title: Hierarchical KV splitter and pipeline-aware memory packing for multi-GPU inference
creator: Avery Patel
description: Problem: As we scale inference across tensor and pipeline parallel configurations, KV cache memory becomes fragmented and unevenly utilized across GPU replicas and pipeline stages. This increases spill-to-host, reduces effective batch size, and complicates continuous batching heuristics. Goal: introduce a hierarchical KV splitter and pipeline-aware memory packing strategy to reduce fragmentation, colocate hot KV slices with stage-local activations, and enable larger continuous batches without violating latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype integrates with runtime allocator and NCCL-based coordination for split placement
p50 per-token generation latency decreases by >=8% at target throughput compared to baseline for 8-GPU tensor+pipeline config
Host spill volume reduced by >=20% for long-context workloads during synthetic trace tests
No correctness regressions across model family (GPT-like causal and encoder-decoder) verified by unit + integration tests
Continuous batching tests show stable latency within SLO at 25% higher batch depth in 95% of synthetic workloads
design_notes: High-level idea: introduce a two-level hierarchy for KV placement: stage-local micro-slices and cross-stage pooled shards. Stage-local micro-slices are small contiguous slabs mapped to the pipeline stage that produced them; pooled shards are larger segments used to store cold or overflow keys.

Memory packing: use micro-slab packing to minimize internal fragmentation. Within each GPU we maintain small fixed-size superblocks (e.g., 1MB) that are subdivided into micro-slices aligned to token KV block sizes (configurable per model). Allocation uses a bump-pointer within active superblocks and a free-list for reclaimed micro-slices.

Interleaving with tensor parallelism: for TP replicas, arrange micro-slices so hot prefixes are replicated across minimal subset of TP replicas required for attention compute, avoiding full replication unless heat metric crosses threshold. Use a lightweight rep-assignment table to track replica ownership.

Pipeline awareness: the allocator receives pipeline stage hints. When a KV entry is produced, runtime attempts to place its micro-slice on the GPU hosting that stage to improve locality for subsequent attention queries that reference local activations.

Prefetch and continuous batching integration: add a batch-coordinator hook to predict hot keys for upcoming micro-batches using short-term frequency counters and recent request traces. Prefetch predictor issues async fetches to local device memory from pooled shards or remote GPUs via NCCL/rccl point-to-point if remote.

Eviction policy: two-tier eviction — evict stage-local cold micro-slices into cross-stage pooled shards first (cheap local memcpy), then spill pooled shards to host pinned memory asynchronously. Hot-key promotion replicates across replicas instead of remote fetch during critical low-latency paths.

Spill strategy and network: asynchronous RDMA/NCCL-based scatter/gather for pooled shard transfers; fallback to host spill if interconnect saturated. Employ backpressure to continuous batching loop when spill queue length is high.

Coordination protocol: use NCCL group ops for barrier syncs only during placement rebalancing to minimize runtime jitter. Background compaction and rebalancing runs on separate threads and yields to inference fast-path.

Compatibility: design supports quantized KV formats and hybrid float/int8 packed slabs; slot meta uses compact headers to avoid expanding memory footprint. Works with both causal and encoder-decoder models but requires stage hint plumbing for encoder-decoder pipeline parallelism.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Rebalancing can introduce jitter during high throughput. Mitigation: background compaction throttled and uses non-blocking NCCL collectives; early exit if batch latency rises beyond threshold.
Risk: Incorrect per-stage hints lead to suboptimal placement. Mitigation: fallback heuristic that places based on access frequency and recent producer/consumer locality if hints absent.
Risk: Network saturation for pooled-shard fetches on shared clusters. Mitigation: rate-limited prefetch + priority queue for hot keys; expose cluster-level config in Dedicated settings.
Risk: Implementation complexity across TP/PP combos. Mitigation: start with a two-stage pipeline+2-way tensor parallel reference and expand to more complex topologies once stable.
benchmarks_expectation: Target workload: long-context chat traces with average sequence length 8k tokens across 8 GPUs (2-stage pipeline x 4 TP replicas)
Memory reduction target: 18-25% decrease in host spill bytes during sustained runs
Latency target: 8-12% improvement in p50 token latency at identical throughput, p95 neutrality (no >10% regressions)
Throughput target: enable safe continuous-batching depth increase of 25% without breaking p95 latency SLO for 90% of synthetic workloads
